title: 5-round AES-192/256 partial-subkey recovery with yoyo/mitm, low data

target.description: Initial AddRoundKey k_-1 followed by 5 AES rounds, with final MixColumns omitted. The algorithm recovers the 128-bit initial subkey k_-1. For the standard 192-/256-bit master keys this is a partial-key target; completing the remaining master-key material is outside the reported budget.

setting.key_relation: One unknown secret key with encryption and decryption oracle access; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: 2^6 chosen plaintext pairs with differences confined to one inverse-shifted column; adaptive decryption of mixture counterparts
assumptions: The source's Section 4.1 explicitly makes the attack descriptions independent of the AES key schedule.
Costs and probability estimates follow the journal version's statistical assumptions; Appendix A.5 identifies rigorous probability analysis as further work.
This record uses the dissection implementation of the MITM matching step; the naive higher-memory table is a separate implementation option.

time.note: Section 4.3 derives fewer than 2^23 encryption equivalents; Table 1 reports the rounded exponent.

data.note: Source's rounded dominant ACC count; the description also encrypts the initial 2^6 pairs. This is not asserted to be an exact sum of all calls.

memory.note: Section 4.3 uses dissection to retain the original 2^9 storage, rather than the naive 2^16-entry MITM table.

preprocessing.note: The source does not separately budget preprocessing for this low-data endpoint.

success.description: The low-data MITM/dissection and naive-table implementations share the Section4.2 source model: one starting pair meets the required round-0 cancellation with probability2^-6. The source does not quantify aggregate recovery for these endpoints; the 64/128-pair fast-endpoint experiments cannot be copied here.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit; construction and parameter-specific defining passages, not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Source model for one starting pair producing zero difference in one shifted column after round0. This is not success for recovering the complete initial subkey.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4 Table 1; pp.15-18, Sections 4.1-4.3 and Algorithm 2.
evidence.interpretation: The record retains the journal version's endpoint and native units. The source's key-schedule-independent recovery of k_-1 is classified as partial recovery for AES-192/256.

evidence.locator: Complete exact primary PDF1–42, all sections, formulas, tables, algorithms, appendices and references.
evidence.interpretation: Complete reading and source inventory; later-literature gates and finite controls separately recorded. No author attack code executed.
All three mixing/retracing-MITM implementations use the same unknown key population; table/dissection/friend extraction is the tuning choice.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.15–18 Sections4.1–4.3, Algorithm2; pp.19–22 Sections4.4–4.5 for the distinct fast endpoint.
evidence.interpretation: The low-data MITM/dissection and naive-table implementations share the Section4.2 source model: one starting pair meets the required round-0 cancellation with probability2^-6. The source does not quantify aggregate recovery for these endpoints; the 64/128-pair fast-endpoint experiments cannot be copied here.

limitations: This record uses the dissection implementation of the MITM matching step; the naive higher-memory table is a separate implementation option.
Numerical costs are source-reported estimates; the attack was not independently implemented or reproduced.
Recovery of the remaining AES-192/256 master-key bits is not assigned the listed partial-subkey costs.
